But the problem seems to be there's a bit of a disconnect between what that means to each of them.For example, Trump's envoys say Russia is, quote, "comfortable" with NATO-like guarantees for Ukraine. Russian officials have pushed back against that idea hard. But President Trump - he says this is all public posturing, that everyone is being much more flexible behind the scenes. We'll just have to see if he's right.MARTIN: And meanwhile, the war continues.MAYNES: It does, and it was staggering losses, particularly from the Russian side, if new findings published yesterday by various independent Russian media in exile is correct. They've been sifting through data that was hacked from Russia's statistics agency and concluded that upwards of an astonishing 700,000 Russian troops have been killed in this war, and those numbers continue to grow.MARTIN: That is NPR's Charles Maynes in Moscow. Charles, thank you.MAYNES: Thank you.

articles.title: Russian incursions into NATO territory are increasing
paragraphs: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte is seeking to reassure the alliance's eastern European members after three Russian cruise missiles landed in Poland on Friday.

SCOTT DETROW, HOST: Russian incursions into NATO territory are increasing. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte is seeking to reassure the alliance's Eastern European members after three Russian cruise missiles landed in Poland on Friday. While no one was hurt, Rutte was in Germany today, where he addressed growing concerns. And for more, we are joined now by Esme Nicholson in Berlin. Hey, Esme.ESME NICHOLSON, BYLINE: Hey, Scott.DETROW: The cruise missiles hit Poland during one of Russia's biggest aerial attacks on Ukraine since the start of the full-scale invasion. Ukraine then hit back over the weekend. So first, bring us up to speed on that.NICHOLSON: Well, as you say, the risks of the war in Ukraine spilling over were loud and clear over the weekend. It started on Friday morning with what Polish authorities have now identified as three Russian cruise missiles striking a rural part of southeastern Poland, about 30 miles from the Ukrainian border. Now, as you say, there were no casualties, but the incursions happened while European forces were staging a military exercise in the region. And Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk calls the incident an "intentional provocation" - that's a quote.Then on Saturday, a sanctioned Russian cargo ship in the Baltic Sea was hit by what is suspected to have been a Ukrainian maritime drone. And on Sunday, Ukraine took credit for sinking a Russian warship docked in the Libyan port of Benghazi, thousands of miles from the front line. Libyan authorities have condemned the attack in their port, reflecting broader concerns that the conflict could spread far beyond Europe.DETROW: Right. And that is a broad battlefield that you're talking about right there. NATO's chief was in Berlin today. Does he view this as the beginning of an escalation beyond Ukraine's borders?NICHOLSON: Well, Rutte was rather cautious in his assessment of the weekend. He was in Berlin for an annual meeting, talking to parliamentarians from NATO countries. And while he acknowledged the danger of cruise missile incursions, he was eager that Polish authorities finish their investigations to establish whether they were intentional or not. Speaking to journalists, he said the alliance has, quote, "many response options" (ph) but that he can't always be open about them. But he also appealed for public support for Ukraine.(SOUNDBITE OF PRESS CONFERENCE)MARK RUTTE: As societies, we have to be resilient and, most importantly, keep that support for Ukraine going. So for every incident in Europe, more support for Ukraine, not less support for Ukraine.NICHOLSON: And Zelenskyy, who dialed into the meeting in Berlin today, urged for fresh negotiations with Russia, this time involving the Europeans.DETROW: Let's talk more about the Europeans. What do you think the odds are that they'll end up playing a role in bringing about the end of this war?NICHOLSON: Well, since last week's coalition of the willing meeting here in Berlin, it's looking a little more likely. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and European leaders warned the U.S. and Russia against going over their heads. And today, Merz stressed that Europe is ready to sit at the table, something U.S. special envoy for peace missions Jared Kushner supports. But Merz also made it clear that no NATO member, quote, "has any interest in an escalation in the Baltic Sea region," which some see as an appeal to Ukraine to do its part to prevent the conflict from spreading.He vowed that European leaders would discuss boosting defense on NATO's eastern flank at an EU summit later this week. And he was also quite candid in stating that NATO made a mistake back in 2008 when it decided not to make Ukraine a member, saying that if Ukraine had been a NATO member, this war would probably have been preventable.DETROW: That is Esme Nicholson in Berlin. Thank you so much.NICHOLSON: Thank you, Scott.

articles.title: Substance released at concert could be linked to robberies, police say
paragraphs: The substance was released near the end of US rapper Don Toliver's gig at Co-op Live on Sunday
An "unknown substance" that prompted a mass evacuation at a rap concert may be linked to robberies and stolen jewellery at the venue, police have said.
More than 12,000 people were evacuated from Manchester's Co-op Live during a performance by US rapper Don Toliver on Sunday.
One person was taken to hospital and 88 others were treated at the scene after concertgoers reported a "horrible smell" and some people "coughing up blood".
Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said officers received nine reports of jewellery being stolen during the concert but no arrests had been made and the substance had not yet been identified.
Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said there was "no wider ongoing risk" to the public.

"We are aware similar robberies have been reported at two European concerts for the same artist and will be linking in with our European counterparts to better understand the wider picture of this suspected offending," he said.
In a statement on Tuesday evening, Co-op Live said it was conducting a "full review" into the incident.

articles.title: BBC and Netflix team up for new CBeebies hub on streamer
paragraphs: Hey Duggee is among the shows which will be part of the CBeebies hub on Netflix
The BBC and Netflix are to launch a trial hub on the streaming service next month, featuring 24 CBeebies shows.
Programmes including Hey Duggee, Numberblocks and Teletubbies can be seen on a branded CBeebies hub on Netflix from 2 December.
The trial's aim is to test new ways for the flagship pre-school channel to reach audiences. The BBC is the UK's largest commissioner of children's content.

BBC iPlayer will remain the home for all CBeebies content. Some CBeebies shows such as Shaun the Sheep are already available on Netflix, but this is the first time they will have a home hub on the subscription streamer.

CBeebies shows will also be made available to Netflix members outside the UK in a distribution deal managed by BBC Studios, with the aim of driving investment into children's content in the UK. The deal does not include China.
Netflix will also commit to funding a small number of new CBeebies commissions, the BBC said.
BBC's chief content officer Kate Phillips said the corporation is "always looking at how we can help more audiences discover" its content and brands.

articles.title: First Children's Booker prize reveals shortlist - and its child judges
paragraphs: The first ever Children's Booker Prize has announced the eight books in the running for the new £50,000 award.
Five novels, two graphic novels and an illustrated collection of short stories are on the shortlist, which is aimed at children aged eight to 12.
The authors in contention include former Children's Laureate of Ireland Eoin Colfer, who is best known for his Artemis Fowl series, and teacher and children's author Catherine Bruton.
Four children have also been announced as new judges after a UK-wide competition. Twelve-year-old Ibrahim from Hampshire was one of those picked from more than 4,000 entrants.
He told me he was called back into school for a phone call with chair of judges Frank Cottrell-Boyce, who broke the news. Ibrahim said he couldn't be happier.
"First Children's Booker Prize judge! On my CV - that's going to take me a long way… I'm too overwhelmed to even be excited."

Cottrell-Boyce told the BBC "it's really, really important that this is a prize for children's books. Having judges who are children will be proof of that… If the children don't love a book, it won't win."

Ibrahim, his fellow child judges and Cottrell-Boyce will be joined on the judging panel by Ghosts and Horrible Histories actor Lolly Adefope and Sanchita Basu De Sarkar, who owns an award-winning children's book shop in north London.

articles.title: Irish reality star dances her way to final of Dancing with the Stars
paragraphs: Maura Higgins is arguably Love Island's biggest success story.

Since leaving the villa in Majorca, Higgins maintained a high profile in the UK, Ireland and across the Atlantic where she has presented Love Island: Aftersun in the US, and was runner up in The Traitors US.
While she failed to find love with Curtis Pritchard in the 2019 series, she may have picked up a few of the ballroom dancer's moves.

The Irish reality TV star has cha cha cha'd her way to the final of Dancing With the Stars on US television, where she will compete with her professional dance partner Mark Ballas, son of Strictly head judge Shirley Ballas.
Higgins and Ballas performed an Ireland-dedicated Paso Doble to Dropkick Murphy's song I'm Shipping up to Boston
From County Longford, there'll be a flavour of Ireland in her dances for the final.
In a video posted to the programme's Instagram page, traditional Irish music can be heard while Higgins and Ballas rehearse.
It will not be the first time on the show Higgins has paid homage to her homeland after she and Ballas performed a Paso Doble to Dropkick Murphy's song I'm Shipping up to Boston.

articles.title: King Charles and Elton John pay tribute to Australian music legend Molly Meldrum
paragraphs: King Charles and Elton John have paid tribute to Australian music industry legend Molly Meldrum, who died aged 83 after a long illness.
Meldrum's family said he "passed away peacefully" at a hospital in Melbourne in the early hours of Monday morning.
The music promoter and broadcaster, born Ian Alexander Meldrum, helped define the nation's music tastes for decades, championing local artists like INXS and Kylie Minogue and global acts like Abba.
Known for his chaotic demeanour and trademark Stetson hat, he interviewed an array of stars, with the king on Monday calling him "a true giant of the music industry".

Born in Victoria in 1943, Meldrum displayed a love of music from an early age and went on to host the Australian Broadcasting Corporation's music television programme Countdown, and later a segment on variety show Hey Hey, It's Saturday.
Meldrum in 2014 became the first person who was not a recording artist to be inducted into the Australian Recording Industry Association (Aria) Hall of Fame.
Meldrum lived with an acquired brain injury after falling from a ladder in 2011.
"Affectionately dubbed 'the Guru', Molly was the heartbeat, the champion and the spirit of Australian music," a statement from Meldrum's family said.

articles.title: From dancing on the Tube to being sectioned: Sabrina Bahsoon on her psychosis misdiagnosis
paragraphs: Sabrina Bahsoon now has more than 900,000 followers across social media
Sabrina Bahsoon became known globally as Tube Girl after self-shot videos of her dancing and lip-syncing on the London Underground blew up online.
The 26-year-old content creator had the world at her feet when she went viral in 2023, going on to build a social media following of more than 900,000 people.
She signed major brand endorsement deals and was pursuing a music career.
But then her "whole life turned upside down" when she had what appeared to be a psychotic episode.
Her symptoms made her violent and erratic, leading to her being sectioned in a mental health hospital - where doctors treated her with anti-psychotic medication.
But Bahsoon's family, helped by her father's neurologist friend, pushed for further tests.
And two months into her hospital treatment, doctors got to the truth.

articles.title: Black Bear Buys Thriller ‘Seeker,’ Starring ‘Obsession’s’ Cooper Tomlinson and ‘Off Campus’ Actor Mika Abdalla (EXCLUSIVE)
paragraphs: Black Bear has acquired “Seeker,” a thriller featuring “Obsession” actor Cooper Tomlinson, “Off Campus” breakout Mika Abdalla and “Happy Death Day” star Jessica Rothe.

The company has North American and U.K. distribution rights to the movie, which was introduced to buyers at this year’s AFM. Directed by Adam Carter Rehmeier and written by Michael Learner, “Seeker” follows Grant (Tomlinson), whose fiancée Caroline (Abdalla) mysteriously disappeared five years earlier. Now a ride-share driver, his life is upended when he picks up a passenger who he is convinced is responsible for her absence. As the logline teases, “What starts as a tense game of cat-and-mouse spirals into something far stranger, more disturbing, and deeply unhinged — challenging everything we think we know.” Related Stories 'Ghost Soldier' Review: Jim Caviezel Is a Superheroic Soldier in an Uninspired, Retrograde Actioner 'The Gospel of Christmas' Review: Tyler Perry's Churchy Musical Drama Does a Threadbare Job of Getting Into the Spirit

“’Seeker’ is exactly the type of bold and propulsive storytelling we look for at Black Bear,” said Katie Anderson, Black Bear’s executive VP of acquisitions. “Michael’s script had us all on the edge of our seats, and with Adam’s singular voice and this cast’s incredible talent, we couldn’t be more excited to bring this film to theaters.”

Alex Lebovici and Michael Learner will produce for Hammerstone Studios, with Adam McKay and Todd Schulman for HyperObject Industries, and Noah Centineo and Enzo Marc of Arkhum Productions. Samuel Hall and Warren Goz will executive-produce for North Five Six, alongside Ibrahim Mohammed, Yasmyne Mohammed, Chase Vergari, Karina Manashil, David Goldman and Andria Spring.

“Seeker” will begin production in January in Washington. The film is fully financed by Hammerstone Studios and Script 2 Screen. North Five Six are representing international distribution rights, with CAA Media Finance having represented U.S. rights.

Black Bear was founded in 2011 as independent production studio and recently launched a domestic distribution arm. The company’s latest theatrical release, the offbeat romantic dramedy “Wicker,” has been a box office winner with $40 million globally to date. Black Bear’s upcoming slate includes Guy Ritchie’s “Wife & Dog,” starring Benedict Cumberbatch and Rosamund Pike; and David Leitch’s “Jason Statham Stole My Bike” led by Statham and Hannah Waddingham. It also recently nabbed Bill Hader’s feature directing debut, “They Know,” a psychological horror film starring Hader and Linda Cardellini.

articles.title: NBC ‘Monitoring’ Storm That Could Ground Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade Balloons: ‘Decisions Will Be Made on Parade Morning’
paragraphs: The 100th celebration of the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City is finding itself at the mercy of the weather gods. It’s made it through rain and even snow, but this time it’s facing an incoming storm that is threatening to bring heavy winds. If things get too windy, the iconic balloons could be grounded.

This would mark the first time since 1971 that the balloons would be grounded. Related Stories 'Heartland' Review: Jessica Chastain Rocks a Stetson and a Swagger for a Soapy Nashville Noir 'Focker-in-Law' Review: Ariana Grande Sporadically Livens Up a Tired Comedy Retread
Balloons are grounded when sustained winds reach 24 mph or wind gusts reach 35 mph. Any decisions regarding balloon flight will be made on parade morning and will be based on weather conditions.
NBC is closely monitoring the weather forecast, with safety being its top priority.
As previously reported, this year’s parade is titled “The Greatest Celebration,” in honor of its centennial anniversary with over 100 floats and 100 balloons.
Among the balloons that are set to take flight are Sorcerer’s Apprentice Mickey and Joe Cool.

“It’s a massive deal for the folks at Disney,” Brendan Kennedy, director of creative production at Macy’s Studio told Variety. “It’s not an IP that generally comes out, except for a huge celebration. It’s our 100th parade, and they were really excited to join us. It was just a joy to get close to Mickey, but the Sorcerer’s Apprentice is so special. It’s that next level of elevated magic that blends really well with Macy’s.”

Another highlight is Snoopy, who returns to the parade in a new role as Joe Cool. “Joe Cool is what happens when Snoopy is pretending to be a student at school. He’s never been in the parade before in this form, which makes it really fun,” Kennedy said. “We’re excited to bring him and Woodstock together. I was on the Parade Studio floor yesterday and saw an arm and an ear being worked on.”

articles.title: ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’: Creating Glenn Close’s Over-the-Top Looks by Leaning Into Drusilla’s ‘Narcissist’ Nature
paragraphs: Being a member of Capitol society in Panem is an honor not to be taken lightly, at least if you’re Drusilla Sickle, played by screen legend Glenn Close in “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.”

In the book, Drusilla is the cruel and vain escort for Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) and the rest of the District 12 tributes in the 50th Hunger Games, where she uses over-the-top fashion to broadcast her social status. Close worked closely with costume designer Bina Daigeler and hair, makeup and prosthetics designer Natalie MacGowan Spencer to ensure the character translated properly from Suzanne Collins’ bestselling prequel novel to the screen. Related Stories A24's 'It Gets Worse' Updates 'Girls' for British Gen Z: TV Review 'Madden' Review: Nicolas Cage Plays John Madden as the Disheveled Buddha of Football in David O. Russell's Eccentric Stunt of a Sports Biopic

One challenge Daigeler faced was meeting Close’s request that each outfit felt connected, creating a through line that explained why Drusilla changes from one look to the next. Despite the drastic differences between each outfit, Daigeler established continuity through the character’s accessories, most notably a collection of gold medals and military-inspired epaulets that created a sense of authority.
“She wears all these medals, because somehow she thinks she is the top general of the capital,” Daigeler tells Variety.
And, not dissimilar to red-bottomed Louboutin shoes, Daigeler gave Drusilla dramatically long black nails that were painted red underneath to show her abundant wealth.

The character’s Capitol allegiance also went beyond her wardrobe, with Spencer overseeing her hair and makeup. While creating the looks, Spencer relied heavily on Collins’ source material to remain faithful to the author’s vision. Collins describes Drusilla as having implanted tabs that pull the skin on her face back, which Spencer wanted to honor. But because there wasn’t enough time each morning for an extensive prosthetics process, Spencer turned to Hollywood tape to tightly pull Close’s skin back, creating a distorted appearance. She later added tabs on the sides of Close’s face to complete the illusion, along with fake teeth that heightened Drusilla’s “scary” and “eerie” appearance.
“[Glenn] really wanted to pull it so taut that it changed all of her facial features, which it really did,” Spencer tells Variety.

Daigeler and Spencer’s shared mission: to create visuals that resonate with the franchise’s devoted fans — who “know their stuff inside out,” Spencer quips. “They’re so passionate.” When the book was released and casting announcements began rolling out, Spencer would regularly check social media to see what fans envisioned for the adaptation and what details they hoped to see on screen.

articles.title: Steven Hack, ‘American Horror Story’ Actor and Original Cast Member of ‘Cats,’ Dies at 68
paragraphs: Steven Hack, an original cast member in the Broadway production of “Cats” who appeared in TV series including “American Horror Story,” died Nov. 19 in Los Angeles following a “sudden and unexpected cardiac event,” Interact Theatre Company confirmed on social media. He was 68.

Hack performed and understudied in multiple roles in “Cats,” including Mungojerrie, Carbucketty, Coricopat, Pouncival and Tumblebrutus. Related Stories 'Hazara Town' Review: A Restrained but Deeply Affecting Doc Portrait of an Afghan Refugee Family Living in Limbo ‘Drummer Boy’ Review: Love, Family and Revolution Conflict at Musket’s Point in a Swoony Period Musical

“It is with great sadness that we share the news that Steven Hack, a founding member of Interact Theatre Company, recently passed away at home following a sudden and unexpected cardiac event,” the company wrote on Instagram.

The post continued, “Steven was a gifted and versatile performer, a superb graphic artist and a cherished member of our artistic family. His creativity and talent helped shape Interact in its earliest years, and his artistry, humor, warmth and generous spirit enriched everything he touched.”

In addition to “Cats,” Hack had an extensive career as an actor with roles in “American Horror Story,” “Ratched,” “Marvel’s Agent Carter,” “Days of Our Lives” and “General Hospital.” Other roles included “Amsterdam,” “Angelyne,” “Pam and Tommy” and “The West Wing.”

He was born in St. Louis before attending college at the California Institute of the Arts and the American Academy of Dramatic Arts. He made his professional debut as one of the teenage dancers in the 1978 film “Grease” before heading to Broadway and accruing a long list of film and television titles.

The company concluded its post, “As we remember Steven, we celebrate not only his many contributions to our company but also the joy of knowing and working with him. He will always hold a special place in Interact’s history and in the hearts of those who knew him. We extend our heartfelt condolences to his family, friends and all who loved him. May his memory be a blessing.”

articles.title: Men’s Wearhouse Kicks Off Black Friday With Designer Discounts on Suits and Tuxedos — Just in Time For Awards Season
paragraphs: If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

Just in time for holiday parties and the upcoming awards season, Men’s Wearhouse has kicked off its Black Friday sale early, slashing prices across its expansive selection of suiting, formalwear and everyday wardrobe staples.

The menswear retailer is offering discounts on top brands such as Calvin Klein, Joseph Abboud, Kenneth Cole and Nautica, with particularly steep savings on sport coats, wool overcoats and tailored separates. Related Stories Brandi Carlile's All-Requests Tour Isn't Just a Magnificent Stunt, but an Unusually Moving Transaction Between Performer and Audience: Concert Review 'Heartland' Review: Jessica Chastain Rocks a Stetson and a Swagger for a Soapy Nashville Noir
The early Black Friday deals, which run through 11:59 p.m. CT on Nov. 24, include 40% off select suits, sport coats and dress shirts, up to 50% off outerwear and casualwear and up to 40% off shoes.

Standout deals include a Calvin Klein slim-fit wool-blend suit for $299.99 and a Joseph Abboud navy wool-blend blazer for $149.99 (normally $249.99). Those looking to spend a little less can snag a classic black Nautica suit for just $119.99, down from $199.99.

The sale also extends to the retailer’s more giftable offerings. Leather belts, ties and dress shirts make practical presents for the men on your list, while those willing to spend a little more can choose from an assortment of dress shoes, loafers and boots.
Shop the full Men’s Wearhouse Black Friday sale here.

articles.title: T-Mobile Kicks Off Holiday Deals With Up to $1,200 Off Apple’s New iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro
paragraphs: If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

T-Mobile is getting an early start on the holiday shopping season, rolling out a slate of new deals on some of the year’s biggest smartphone releases, including Apple‘s new iPhone 18 Pro and its first-ever foldable phone, the iPhone Duo.

The wireless carrier is offering up to $1,200 off both devices with qualifying trade-ins on select plans, along with the option for eligible customers to walk away with a new phone for $0 upfront. Related Stories 'Ghost Soldier' Review: Jim Caviezel Is a Superheroic Soldier in an Uninspired, Retrograde Actioner ‘Dig’ Review: Amy Poehler’s Archeology Comedy Is Shockingly Unfunny
The offers arrive just weeks after Apple introduced its latest iPhone lineup in September, with the iPhone Duo representing the company’s most significant design departure in years.

Released Oct. 23, the iPhone Duo marks Apple’s long-awaited entry into the foldable smartphone market, joining competitors including Samsung and Google. The device features a 5.4-inch exterior screen that unfolds into a 7.6-inch display — the largest ever on an iPhone — designed for watching videos, gaming and multitasking across apps. The foldable design also makes it the thinnest iPhone Apple has released when opened. It’s currently available in Star White and Night Sky

Meanwhile, the iPhone 18 Pro, which arrived Sept. 18, introduces Apple’s first variable-aperture camera, allowing users to adjust depth of field and lighting directly in the Camera app. The device also features a new 48-megapixel Fusion Main camera, Apple’s A20 Pro chip, an upgraded cooling system and enhanced AI capabilities through iOS 27. Available in Black, Silver, Glacier and Burgundy, the Pro starts at $1,199.

Beyond Apple’s newest releases, T-Mobile’s early holiday promotions include $830 off the iPhone 17, offers on the iPhone 16 and 17e that can cover the full device cost, and discounts on Android devices including the Samsung Galaxy S26 series, Google Pixel 11 lineup and Motorola Razr. You can also get four lines right now for just $25/line and get four iPhone 17e devices “on us” when you switch.

articles.title: Pochettino leads Man Utd fury at Yoro red card ruling
paragraphs: Manchester United defender Leny Yoro (second left) is shown a red card by referee Sam Barrott at Anfield
Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has questioned the competence of video assistant referee officials after defender Leny Yoro had his red card overturned by the Football Association.
Yoro was sent off eight minutes into United's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday after bringing down Aleksander Isak just outside the United penalty area.

United sources say they have conclusive proof it was impossible for Isak to reach the ball after he took a heavy touch, that it would have run on to goalkeeper Senne Lammens and Yoro should not have been punished for denying a goalscoring opportunity.
Pochettino said he had some sympathy with referee Sam Barrott but he is livid at how the situation played out.
"I am very disappointed," the Argentine said. "This type of thing can never happen.

"We can accept the referee can make a mistake. But if we have VAR, what were they doing? What were they doing? Are we going to repeat the game? Are we going to have the possibility to play 11 by 11? No.
"We have an unbelievable car, but we need to be at the level to drive [it]. We accept that the technology is there but what are they doing?"

articles.title: Sooryavanshi, 15, breaks sixes record by scoring 204 off 53 balls
paragraphs: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi made his T20 international debut for India in July but is yet to play a one-day international
India's 15-year-old batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hit the most sixes ever recorded in a senior men's innings in blazing 204 from 53 balls for India A against the United Arab Emirates.

While almost halving the record for the fastest double-century in List A cricket, Sooryavanshi hit 28 sixes and seven fours in the Asia Cup Rising Stars competition - easily breaking Chad Bowes' previous record of 103 balls from 2024.
The teenage opener also broke the record for the fastest century and 150, the latter of which he already held, before being caught at long-off with his side five runs from victory.
India A ultimately passed their target of 250, played against a UAE side that featured a number of internationals but was not their current first-choice side, in 14.2 overs in Doha.
Sooryavanshi now holds the following records in List A cricket, the categorisation given to senior one-day matches:
Fastest fifty: 11 balls v Sri Lanka A, 21 June (previously Kaushalya Weeraratne, 12 balls, 1 November 2005)
Fastest hundred: 28 balls, today (previously Jake Fraser-McGurk, 29 balls, 8 October 2023)

articles.title: Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners - 10 months after tournament
paragraphs: Sadio Mane's Senegal have been confirmed as Afcon 2025 winners following their appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, giving the Teranga Lions a second continental title
Senegal have been reinstated as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations after a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport.
The court's award overturns a previous decision which had stripped the West Africans of the title they won on the pitch during a chaotic final against host nation Morocco in January.

With the game goalless, Senegal left the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest at a penalty awarded against them. The match in Rabat was delayed by over 15 minutes before Morocco's Brahim Diaz had his spot-kick saved.
Senegal then triumphed 1-0 after extra time, with Pape Gueye scoring the winner.

That result was overturned almost two months later when a Confederation of African Football (Caf) appeals board decreed the Teranga Lions had breached competition regulations by leaving the field of play after the penalty was awarded.

Senegal's football federation (FSF) subsequently appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas), sport's highest legal authority, with a three-man panel hearing its case behind closed doors in Lausanne on 8 October.

In a unanimous verdict, the Cas panel has effectively backed the decision by referee Jean-Jacques Ndala to restart the game after Senegal returned to the field and the match was played to a conclusion. The result of the final stands and Senegal are now confirmed as Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) 2025 winners.

articles.title: 'I miss being on court' - Sinner has 'minor surgery' on knee
paragraphs: Jannik Sinner attended a ceremony for players who had become world number one at the ATP Finals in Turin
World number two Jannik Sinner says he has had "minor surgery" on his knee, just seven weeks before January's Australian Open begins.
The five-time Grand Slam champion has not played competitively since winning Wimbledon on 12 July.
In a post on Instagram, Sinner said he had undergone surgery to "improve the condition of my iliotibial band" - a thick band of tissue that runs along the outside of the knee.
"Over the past few months, together with my team we've tried everything to treat my injury without surgery," the 25-year-old wrote.
"After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn't respond as we'd all hoped.
"I really miss being on court and will now begin my recovery process together with my team."
Earlier in November, Sinner said his goal was to go to Australia and potentially "play a few tournaments" before the first Grand Slam of the year begins on 17 January.

articles.title: A world-class winger - Louis Rees-Zammit 2.0
paragraphs: Wales wing Louis Rees-Zammit has impressed since returning to rugby union from a stint in American Football
Australia wing Harry Potter had Louis Rees-Zammit exactly where he wanted him.
As Wales attacked in Cardiff on Saturday, Potter showed Rees-Zammit the outside – a four-metre channel between him and the touchline.
The touchline is a defender's best friend. An extra defender. The edge of the cliff. It would take something extraordinary to beat Potter without running out of ground.

A shake of the hips and a change of direction later, Potter was diving like a cricketer in the outfield, grasping at thin air. Rees-Zammit was on his way to setting up a wonderful try for Blair Murray.
Rees-Zammit has been turning heads for years. On the pitch with his pace, off it with his pristine teeth and pop star looks.
But it wasn't raw speed that had left Potter on the turf.
Alex Cuthbert knows a thing or two about running. A former national-level 400m runner and British and Irish Lions wing, he spent much of his rugby career working on his technique.

articles.title: FA chief signs NDA to view Fifa sell-off plot documents
paragraphs: Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt has signed a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) as a condition of viewing documents related to Fifa president Gianni Infantino's failed World Cup sell-off plot.
Hewitt was granted access to the information at the world governing body's headquarters in Zurich.

Earlier this month, Fifa said "key documents" on the abandoned plan to sell stakes in its tournaments to private investors would be made available to members of its council, but only in person and under "strict review protocols to preserve confidentiality".
Uefa had demanded Fifa release details about the controversial Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, and answer questions relating to its decision-making.

Hewitt was among a group of council members who wrote to Fifa to say they were "concerned that any review would seemingly be limited to certain 'key documents'… which in turn would only be available for review under unknown 'strict review protocols'".
They also asked for clarity on what the protocols were, and "an explanation as to why Fifa considers such restrictions necessary since it is not clear why our rights are being limited in such a way".
The NDA means Hewitt cannot reveal what she has read, or comment about it publicly.

Fair Square, which campaigns for greater accountability in sport, told BBC Sport: "Debbie Hewitt and the FA didn't need to see the details of FFE to know that it was a gross abuse of presidential power.

articles.title: Rayan Cherki magic denies Napoli but Manchester City’s struggles continue
paragraphs: This was the perfect snapshot of Manchester City’s autumn difficulties. They simply cannot keep the door shut and looked like being picked off by Napoli, who had scored through Rasmus Højlund and Noa Lang either side of Ayyoub Bouaddi’s equaliser. Then Rayan Cherki, insistent but frustrated for most of the evening, seized the mantle five minutes from time and earned a welcome but deeply flawed draw. It meant Kevin De Bruyne, whose return last season had been ill-starred, was denied a deserved victory on his old home turf.

The buildup was largely a homage to De Bruyne, who was serenaded at the end of the warm-up and cheered upon the announcement of his name. It had all been done 14 months previously too, although back then De Bruyne lasted only 26 minutes, when a red card to Giovanni Di Lorenzo brought his sacrifice and an eventual 2-0 defeat. There have been few like the Belgian and his latest return was a luscious reminder, in these heavily asterisked times, of garlands collected under the same grim cloud.

In truth neither City nor a creaky Napoli, who are eighth in Serie A and functional rather than flowing, are the alluring propositions of days past. Beyond the De Bruyne appreciation ritual and a vocal performance from the visitors’ upper-tier contingent, this latest procedural wedge of league phase content commenced to near silence. City’s emergence in a new all-orange kit, apparently earmarked for selected Champions League games and timed handily for the festive season, added a degree of visual warmth to the late November chill.

Maresca needs his own tenure, stuttering amid selection uncertainties and questions over the team’s balance as well as the looming elephant, to catch light. Within a minute of kick-off Elliot Anderson came close to providing the spark with a low 20-yarder that Vanja Milinkovic-Savic parried unconvincingly. Anderson, scorer of a superb volley in Saturday’s otherwise laboured draw with Fulham, had kept his place in a side showing five changes.

City threatened again when Nico O’Reilly headed over at the far post and, even though Josko Gvardiol needed sound timing to stop a marauding Matteo Politano down the right, it was clear enough Napoli’s menace would not exceed the sporadic. As the half-hour approached Højlund shot tamely at Gianluigi Donnarumma from an angle but the concern for a ponderous City was that, since those early exchanges, they had shown little suggestion of conjuring a breakthrough. A considered ball in from Anderson, missed by a karate-kicking Erling Haaland, offered thin gruel.

Anderson sought Haaland again with a delivery that was shovelled behind for a corner. Napoli had hardly oozed composure but City’s speed of thought and movement had been too slow. When De Bruyne, manning the midfield alongside Scott McTominay and Billy Gilmour, fumbled possession inside his own half the hosts lacked sufficient zip to take advantage.
Kylian Mbappé scored twice as Real Madrid overturned a half-time deficit to thrash PSV Eindhoven 5-1 and move three points clear at the top of the Champions League table overnight.

José Mourinho’s side trailed to Ivan Perisic’s 32nd-minute penalty, but Federico Valverde fired them level early in the second period. Jude Bellingham scored Real’s second with a sumptuous finish from outside the box and two clinical finishes from Mbappé extended his side’s 100% start to the competition this season to five matches before Vinícius Júnior (pictured congratulating Mbappé) added their fifth goal.

articles.title: Dortmund’s Beier halts Arsenal charge after thunderbolt from Gyökeres
paragraphs: Arsenal’s sky-high standards are slipping. For the second time in four days, Mikel Arteta’s side found themselves a goal up at half-time and apparently cruising towards victory, only for their opponents to rouse themselves and earn a deserved draw. After Newcastle on Saturday, this time it was an impressive Borussia Dortmund who became only the second side to take points off Arsenal in their past 15 group stage games in this competition.

It could have been worse had an offside flag not ruled out Jobe Bellingham’s goal after Max Beier equalised a thunderbolt from Viktor Gyökeres. But the much-maligned Sweden striker was guilty of a glaring miss late on as Arsenal laid siege to Dortmund’s goal, with the German side having to hang on for a result that gave their travelling fans a night to remember. A frustrated Arteta will know his side must be more clinical when Real Madrid and Jude Bellingham visit north London in a fortnight.

While Max Dowman and Ethan Nwaneri – on loan at Dortmund from the Gunners – had to make do with a place on their respective benches, the exploits of another teenager were on the Arsenal supporters’ lips on their way to the ground. A stunning solo goal from 14-year-old Luis Muñoz – an England Under-15 international who is the youngest player ever to feature in the Uefa Youth League – against Dortmund earlier in the day showed that Arsenal’s conveyor belt of talent continues to produce.

Aside from Myles Lewis-Skelly – a relative veteran these days at 20 – Arteta opted for experience as he made six changes from the draw against Newcastle on Saturday, including Kepa Arrizabalaga deputising in goal for the injured David Raya.

Dortmund haven’t been crowned German champions since Jürgen Klopp’s days in 2012 but lead the Bundesliga by two points from Bayern Munich. Like Arsenal, Niko Kovac’s side has relied on a solid defence and the Croatian manager attempted to stiffen his midfield by selecting Joey Veerman alongside Jobe Bellingham and ahead of their exciting Greece teenager, Konstantinos Karetsas.

Como sit third in the table for now after securing their fourth win in the competition, 1-0 at home against AEK Athens, thanks to Luis Milla’s spectacular second-half winner. Lucas Da Cunha, the Como captain, missed a first-half penalty.

articles.title: Gul takes pain for buoyant Galatasaray to condemn Aston Villa to Champions League loss
paragraphs: This was Aston Villa’s third trip to Istanbul in the calendar year but, this time, they departed with different emotions. Unlike on the banks of the Bosphorus at Besiktas Park in May, the scene of their unforgettable Europa League triumph, or at Fenerbahce in January, they came away with a bloody nose. Galatasaray’s match-winner, Deniz Gul, finished with similar, the substitute requiring a bandage after bravely taking a boot to the face from Nicolas Jackson as the hosts rippled the net on 77 minutes. It was the game’s first effort on target, Galatasaray maintaining their commanding form on home soil to extend Villa’s winless run to six matches in all competitions.

On the outside, this is a gladiatorial arena, a giant spaceship parked on Ali Sami Yen complex. But inside there is a poor pitch that began cutting up during the warm-up. John McGinn, one of four changes from Villa’s stalemate with Sunderland on Saturday, gestured towards the turf in frustration after a through ball went awry, but nobody of a Villa persuasion could blame defeat on the surface. As Unai Emery had stated, it was the same for both teams.

Villa were again blunt in attack and did not do enough to claim victory. A livid Emery was booked for his protests at the German officials during five minutes of stoppage time. “I’m a little bit disappointed,” said the Villa manager, who earlier fumed at the delay in Leon Goretzka being allowed to replace João Gomes. “After their goal, it was impossible to play, they were wasting time, they were on the field, the referee was not helping. They added only five minutes: ‘OK, finish the match, we don’t want to play more?’ I don’t think the referee was fair with us.”

The Feyenoord midfielder Oussama Targhalline’s early own goal was enough to clinch Porto a 1-0 win in Rotterdam and Cucho Hernández scored twice as Real Betis won 2-0 at Slovan Bratislava. Press Association

articles.title: Jannik Sinner’s Australian Open appearance in doubt after knee surgery
paragraphs: ‘We’ve tried everything to treat injury without surgery’

Jannik Sinner faces further time off the court after undergoing knee surgery. The former world No 1 has been sidelined with pain in his right knee since winning his second consecutive Wimbledon title in July.

Details on Sinner’s condition have been scarce but on Tuesday he announced he has had a minor operation on his iliotibial band in an attempt to solve the problem. While no timeline for recovery has yet been set out, it seems almost certain to rule out a comeback for the Australian Open in January, as had been the intention.

Sinner said in a statement: “Over the past few months, together with my team, we’ve tried everything to treat my injury without surgery. After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn’t respond as we had all hoped, that’s why today I underwent a minor surgery to improve the condition of my iliotibial band. I really miss being on court and will now begin my recovery process together with my team.”
The iliotibial band is a thick band of fibrous connective tissue running down the outside of the thigh, and injuries associated with it are typically caused by overuse.

Sinner set a record by winning the first five Masters 1000 tournaments of the year, becoming only the second man after Novak Djokovic to complete the career Golden Masters. But he appeared exhausted in suffering a shock early loss at the French Open before rebounding strongly at Wimbledon. His absence has allowed Alexander Zverev to overtake him at the top of the rankings, while Carlos Alcaraz is now close behind in third after a hugely impressive comeback from his own injury issues.
The operation was carried out by Professor Lasse Lempainen, a Finnish specialist in orthopaedic surgery.

articles.title: Cowan-Dickie insists England will not let up after record triumph over All Blacks
paragraphs: Luke Cowan-Dickie is adamant England will not let complacency creep in after their record win over the All Blacks, insisting they will not repeat the mistakes of the 2019 World Cup.

Cowan-Dickie is one of three players, with Jamie George and Maro Itoje, who would claim a fourth career win for England against New Zealand on Saturday if Steve Borthwick’s side back up last weekend’s 37-12 victory at Twickenham. The Sale hooker was part of the squad who defeated the All Blacks in the 2019 World Cup semi-final in emphatic fashion and went into the final against South Africa as favourites. Eddie Jones’s side were comfortably outplayed by the Springboks, however, with Cowan-Dickie acknowledging that England failed to hit their emotional peak that day.

Last weekend England flew out of the blocks, inspired by having Lewis Moody at the point of their V-formation response to the haka, and Cowan-Dickie is convinced there will be no complacency against the wounded All Blacks. Borthwick gave the players Monday off before resuming training on Tuesday.

Cowan-Dickie said: “Back then was the semi-final of the World Cup, maybe we left too much emotion out there and didn’t take enough into the final? Could we learn anything from that? Maybe little parts, complacency? Maybe that’s a big one. But the way we trained today, I don’t see any complacency. The boys are as up for it as they were last week.

“It’s a difficult one, I don’t know if we were complacent, it’s just the amount of emotion that went into that semi-final game, did we build the emotions back up for that final? The team we’ve got now is completely different. There are a lot of younger boys involved and they’re frothing at the bit. Obviously Lewis last week added that little bit but, for me, it’s a Test match. If we were playing tomorrow I’d be ready to go.”

Meanwhile, England’s wing sensation Will Joseph has revealed he has been receiving advice from his elder brother, Jonathan – who won 54 caps for his country – after proving Borthwick’s find of the autumn. Joseph won his first cap in 2022 but had to wait four years for a second, in which he scored a record-equalling five tries, earlier this month.

“It’s definitely been a whirlwind, it’s been pretty surreal. I’m quite literally pinching myself,” he said. “It’s very useful having [Jonathan]. I feel like everything I’m going through or experiencing, he definitely would have experienced. He also knows the game inside out, so he’s very supportive. He tells me bits he sees in my game and stuff I can improve on so he’s very useful to have as a brother.”

articles.title: Gukesh escapes time crisis to draw world chess championship opener with Sindarov
paragraphs: Indian chess star Gukesh Dommaraju held off Javokhir Sindarov amid a mounting time crisis on Tuesday, drawing the opening game of their eagerly awaited $2.5m world title match in 38 moves at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in the picturesque Geneva suburb of Cologny.

After spending more than 36 minutes on a single move and much of the afternoon racing against the clock, the defending champion said the time he invested early helped him play faster as a drawish position sharpened and his minutes dwindled opposite the in-form Uzbek challenger. “When I got into the time trouble, I’d already thought about the next few moves,” Gukesh said. “And then the moves after that were pretty easy.”

India’s Gukesh Dommaraju is defending his world chess championship against fast-rising Uzbek grandmaster Javokhir Sindarov in the youngest world title match in chess history. The best-of-14-games contest is set to take place from 24 November to 12 December at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny, overlooking Lake Geneva, with both players aged 20 when the first move is played.

Gukesh became the youngest undisputed world chess champion in history when he defeated China’s Ding Liren in December 2024, aged 18, shattering the previous record held by Garry Kasparov, who was 22 when he dethroned Anatoly Karpov in 1985. An aggressive player known for creating sharp, tactically complex positions aimed at unsettling opponents, the Chennai-born grandmaster has struggled badly for form since winning the title, plummeting to No 26 in the world rankings from a career-high No 3 after an extended string of underwhelming performances, raising doubts over his chances of retaining the crown in his first title defense.

Sindarov, roughly six months older than Gukesh, stunned the chess establishment with a commanding performance at this year’s eight-man Candidates tournament in Cyprus, finishing unbeaten with six wins and eight draws against a stacked field that included Fabiano Caruana, Hikaru Nakamura and Anish Giri. Known for his cool-headed precision and ability to mine advantages from seemingly quiet positions, the Tashkent-born grandmaster has climbed into the world’s top five after a breakthrough year that included winning the 2025 Fide World Cup in Goa. He is the first player from Uzbekistan to challenge for the world championship.

The match consists of 14 classical games, with one point awarded for a win and a half-point for a draw. The first player to reach 7½ points wins the title. Each player has 120 minutes for the first 40 moves, followed by 30 minutes for the remainder of the game, with a 30-second increment per move starting at move 41. Players cannot agree to a draw before black’s 40th move.

If the match is tied 7-7 after 14 games, a series of faster tiebreaks will decide the champion: first four rapid games (15 minutes plus 10 seconds per move), then two rapid games (10 minutes plus five seconds), followed if necessary by two blitz games (three minutes plus two seconds). If still tied, single blitz games will be played, alternating colors, until one player wins.
